info.name: Life Planner API
info.description: Full endpoint collection for the Life Planner backend (user-api :4000 and admin-api :4001), covering the base spec plus Addendum 2: task privacy, board sharing, flexible (non-date) tasks, the nutrition board, the budget tracker, and admin moderation + analytics. Import the companion environment 'Life Planner (Local)'. Run Auth > Login and Admin API > Admin login first to populate tokens; most requests auto-save the ids they create. Folder 22 collects the expected-failure cases so the guard rails are easy to re-verify.

request.description: Liveness check (not under /api/v1).
Creates a user, seeds default categories + settings, returns tokens. Tokens auto-saved to env.
Use the seeded demo user (demo@lifeplanner.local / demo12345) or the one you registered. Tokens auto-saved.
Rotates the refresh token. New tokens auto-saved.
country pre-fills the food-catalog filter on the nutrition board.
Revokes all other sessions and returns a fresh token pair.
Always answers identically whether or not the email exists. The reset token prints to the server console when MAIL_TRANSPORT=console.
Paste the token from the server console into the resetToken environment variable.
categoryId is optional; remove it if you don't have one saved.
Creates one activity per day in the range. excludeWeekends or daysOfWeek:[1,2,3] filter days.
Empty body flips isDone. Send {"isDone": true} to force a value.

request.description: Non-date-specific task: not locked to a single day, tracked toward targetCount completions within the window.
activeOn is optional — narrows to flexible tasks whose window contains that date.
For flexible tasks only. Increments completedCount toward targetCount; auto-marks isDone once the target is reached. Use the regular toggle endpoint for dated tasks instead.
Audit trail. Admin-initiated deletions appear here as DELETED_BY_ADMIN with the acting adminId.

Each day carries a read-only importedEvents overlay from connected calendars. Kept separate from activities: not editable, no quota, no streak effect — total and done ignore them. Owner-only; a shared board returns an empty list even with a FULL grant.
Set tagId in the environment (copy an id from List tags).
The hourly materializer job creates concrete activities from this RRULE up to RECURRING_HORIZON_DAYS.
remindAt must be ISO 8601. The per-minute dispatcher sends due PENDING reminders (mail prints to the console by default).
Returns a tokenized, public .ics URL. Open it in a browser or paste into a calendar app.
Invalidates the old .ics URL and mints a new one.
REST fallback. Real-time delivery is over WebSocket (see the TESTING guide).
PUT replaces the whole document; unknown keys are rejected (.strict()).
Auth is optional here: send the Authorization header if the user is logged in (attaches userId), omit it for anonymous/pre-login visits. Rate-limited more tightly than general traffic.
Owner-initiated; permission is PUBLIC_ONLY (default) or FULL (includes private tasks). Re-inviting the same viewer updates the existing grant.
Requires an ACTIVE BoardShare where :id is the owner and I'm the viewer. Private tasks are included only if my permission is FULL.
Revocation is a status flip, not a delete — revoked grants stay auditable.
Replaces the whole selection — the natural shape for a multi-select 'available foods' widget.
Only PUBLISHED plans are ever visible to the user; a DRAFT plan the admin is still building returns 404.
404 until Set estimated income has been called for this month.

A month no longer carries a single estimatedIncome figure. Income is a list of rows (folder 42); this endpoint now only sets the month note. The old summary still returns estimatedIncome as a deprecated alias of totalIncome so existing clients do not break — move to GET /ledger.
Expenses now carry COMMITTED vs PAID so they line up with projected vs arrived income. Defaults to COMMITTED.
Expenses now carry COMMITTED vs PAID so they line up with projected vs arrived income. Defaults to COMMITTED.

Kept for backwards compatibility. estimatedIncome here is a deprecated alias of totalIncome. New clients should use GET /budget/:year/:month/ledger, which returns income rows, expense rows and all totals in one call.

Seeded SUPERADMIN. Tokens auto-saved to adminAccessToken/adminRefreshToken.
Set userId in the environment (copy from a conversation's user, or the demo user id).
Admin-scoped calendar view: includes isPrivate activities unconditionally, no BoardShare required.
Also revokes every refresh token the user holds.
Soft-deletes the activity and records an admin-attributed ActivityHistory entry.
Page views, unique visitors (distinct sessionId), new signups, active users.
Context for building the meal plan: what the user says is available to them.
Full replace of the day's plan. Flip status to PUBLISHED once the plan is ready for the user to see.
Flexible tasks use /progress. Expect 400 NOT_A_DATED_TASK.
Dated tasks use /toggle. Expect 400 NOT_A_FLEXIBLE_TASK.

request.description: Paystack inside Africa, Paddle elsewhere. Region-specific prices win over the region:"" fallback.
Requires live Paddle/Paystack keys. Entitlement is NEVER granted here — only the webhook grants it.
Apple/Google deep-link to the store; Paddle returns a hosted portal; Paystack is managed in-app.
Cancels at period end so the person keeps what they paid for.
The client posts the store receipt; the server verifies with Apple/Google before granting. Set VERIFY_STORE_RECEIPTS=false to test without store keys.
Mobile reports the store front it is signed into; web reports its own guess. Drives both the food catalog and the checkout rails.
Height and year of birth double as the calorie/fitness context an admin needs when authoring a meal plan.
Local storage driver serves from /media; switch STORAGE_DRIVER=r2 for Cloudflare.
Selecting a preset clears any uploaded photo, and vice versa.
SUPPORT is reachable on every tier; LIFE_COACH and FITNESS are Pro-only and come back locked:true for Free users.

Hidden from the user immediately; readable by oversight for 30 days, then permanently purged by the cron job.

request.description: 400 for a flexible task, 409 if one is already running.
Case-insensitive across activity title/description, goal title/description and day-note content. Private activities ARE included — this route never crosses a user boundary.
Authored by an admin, not generated. Returns null when nothing has been written for the range.
Clears the flag on every other goal in the same transaction, so exactly one is featured.
Restores DEFAULT_SETTINGS from shared-utils. Timezone is a fact about the person, not a preference, so it is preserved.

PUBLISHED only — a DRAFT never reaches the user.
403/402 when mealPlansEnabled is false. Surfaces in the admin queue.
Imported events are a read-only ImportedEvent overlay — never Activity rows. They are not editable, do not count toward quota and do not affect streaks.

Unauthenticated. Same shape as GET /subscription/plans plus resolvedFrom — one buildPlanCatalog() serves both, so public and signed-in pricing cannot drift.

request.description: Reads cf-ipcountry, x-vercel-ip-country, fastly-client-country or x-country-code. No geo-IP service is called. Cloudflare XX is treated as unknown.

request.description: Two-letter ISO codes only. An unknown-but-valid code such as AQ returns the fallback catalog rather than an error.
A coach only ever sees the conversation types they staff, plus unassigned work. assigned=any is Manager/Super Admin only.
Manager and Super Admin only. Returns soft-deleted messages and every prior version of an edited one. A coach passing the same flag silently gets the normal view.
The receiving admin must actually staff this conversation type, or 400.
Refuses a target that lacks the role, or one already at maxClients.
The user accepts in one tap; acceptance still respects their quota.

request.description: Run this before checkout. An address that already pays for Pro is refused with a message telling them to cancel first, so we never take money we cannot honour. An unknown address is fine — that person simply gets an emailed invitation. Max 2 beneficiaries (3 seats including the payer).
beneficiaryEmails is re-validated server-side; the count must equal seats - 1.

history holds invitations that lapsed or were declined, so the payer understands why a seat freed up. A declined invite reads as DECLINED whether the person simply said no or reported it as unsolicited — that distinction is deliberately invisible to the payer.
Refused when the plan has no spare capacity.
An unclaimed invite is pulled immediately; an active seat ends at period end, because it was paid for.
Lets someone see who invited them before signing up.
Refused if the claimer already pays for their own Pro.

Deliberately unauthenticated: the person clicking may have no account, and requiring a login to disown an action you never took would be absurd. The one-time token is the credential and only ever reaches the mailbox the notice went to. canReject is true only for invitations — declining an invite is not an accusation.
Cancels the invitation. Innocent — no report is filed.

item.name: Report — I did not do this

request.description: Consequences by type: SIGNUP suspends the imposter account and ends every session; PASSWORD_RESET voids outstanding reset links and ends sessions; SEAT_INVITE cancels the invitation. All three land in the admin abuse queue. Tokens are single-use and live 30 days.
A report button that goes nowhere would be worse than none, so reports queue here for a human.
One report is noise; the same sender reported repeatedly is a pattern.
Currency, payment provider and tax rate per country. This is what makes charging Lagos differently from London an ops change rather than a deploy.
taxRate only applies where we are merchant of record (Paystack). Paddle and the app stores remit on our behalf.

request.description: One call for the whole budget screen: income rows, expense rows and every total. The server owns the arithmetic so two clients can never disagree about a balance. Filters narrow the returned lists but never change the totals — a filter is a view, not a redefinition of the month.
The "what do I actually have?" view.
title and amount are required; description, source and expectedDate are optional. expectedDate must fall inside the month.

request.description: Logging money already banked should not need a two-step create-then-mark.
Silently materialises PROJECTED copies into the next three months. The horizon is deliberately not surfaced to the user — they asked for a recurring salary, not a lecture about horizons.
The most-used control on the budget screen. Pass receivedAt to back-date it.
Reversible, because people mis-tap.

The original is marked DEFERRED and stays put; a fresh PROJECTED copy appears in the target month flagged rolledOver. Moving the row instead would erase the fact that it was expected here and slipped — which is exactly the information that makes the view realistic. Only forwards, and only once.
Status changes go through the dedicated endpoints, not a blind PATCH.
Mirrors arrived/projected on the income side so the comparison means something.
Incomes land as PROJECTED and expenses as COMMITTED — copying "paid" forward would assert something that has not happened. Cancelled incomes are not resurrected.

Backs the first-run "re-populate from a recent month" chooser in one call instead of three ledger fetches. Months with no data come back with hasData:false rather than being omitted, so the chooser can show "June (empty)".

A ledger is a view of a month, not a resource that must exist. An untouched month returns 200 with empty lists, zeroed totals and started:false — the empty state renders a budget, not an error. GET /budget/:y/:m still 404s, since that addresses the month record itself.
Admin eyes only. Written by staff about the person; no user-facing endpoint selects this column.
Replaces the whole list, so ordering stays under the console's control.
Filters: q, status (incl. DELETED), subscription (FREE|PRO|EXPIRED), country, joinedFrom/joinedTo.

request.description: weeks accepts 8, 12 or 26. Deltas compare the trailing seven days against the seven before.
Temporary and explained: the user is shown the reason and when it lifts. Defaults to 7 days — an open-ended suspension is a ban wearing a different hat. Pass `until` for an explicit ISO date.
Permanent and unexplained to the account. The reason is stored for staff and visible here, but never returned to the banned user.
Adds a REINSTATED event; it does not erase the earlier ones.
Immutable audit trail. User.status is current state; this is history, and it is what the banned/suspended charts count from.
Scopes every counter and series to that calendar month and buckets it by week. The delta then compares against the previous month, not last week.
Returns both currencies and how many selected meals would be removed, so the UI can warn before anything is destroyed.
Refused with 400 unless confirm is true. Clears selected meals and switches currency. Historic budget amounts are not rewritten — only the symbol changes.
App Store Connect → App Information → Server Notifications V2. Verified against the x5c leaf certificate with the chain root pinned to APPLE_ROOT_CA_G3. Idempotent on notificationUUID.
Play Console → Monetisation setup → Pub/Sub topic. The shared token is a first gate; the real guard is that every notification is re-verified against the Play Developer API before it grants anything.
Response is { deleted: true }, not { ok: true }. Ownership is checked through the parent goal, so another account gets 404 rather than 403.
Composes with ?status=. Still scoped by userId, so another account’s activity id returns an empty list.
New canonical form, matching income and /paid. The unscoped /budget/expenses/:id still works.
hero/features/faqs sit on data directly, NOT under data.content. Arrays are never null. Editable from the admin console.
